methods.name: Natural History Quiz
methods.note: Quiz in the Varrock Museum basement. A one-off 1,000 XP takes you from level 1 to 9 with no requirements. Krystilia turns away a level 1 slayer.

methods.name: Krystilia (Wilderness)
methods.note: Edgeville. Wilderness-only tasks worth 25 points each. Any combat level, so she can assign hard tasks, but not to a level 1 slayer. Only risk gear you can lose.

methods.name: Turael
methods.note: Burthorpe. Easy, fast tasks but poor XP and no points. Used to start out, to boost points between milestone tasks and to swap out a bad task.

methods.name: Mazchna
methods.note: Canifis. 6 points a task. A step up from Turael and usable for point boosting.

methods.name: Vannaka
methods.note: Edgeville Dungeon. 8 points a task. Can assign tough tasks like blue dragons at low level, so leave combat level checking on.

methods.name: Chaeldar
methods.note: Zanaris. 10 points a task. Where the guide says a mid-level account at 70 combat can start.

methods.name: Konar quo Maten
methods.note: Mount Karuulm. 18 points a task and each task is tied to one location. Use her for milestone tasks. Assigns hydras, as does Mortimer.

methods.name: Nieve or Steve
methods.note: Tree Gnome Stronghold. 12 points a task. Similar list to Duradel with a few weaker tasks such as brine rats and scabarites.

methods.name: Duradel
methods.note: Shilo Village. Best master, 15 points a task. Our estimate with no cannon and every task done: burst dust devils, nechryael and smoke devils, melee the rest.

methods.name: Duradel with cannon and barrage
methods.note: Our estimate from the guide: cannon, venator bow and barrage, six tasks blocked, every other task done. Skipping all but its best tasks nears 75k but costs points.

methods.name: Mortimer
methods.note: Wyrmscraig Cavern, reached part-way through Fallen From Grace. Choose from two tasks, three after 50. No points without a modifier. Jagex puts his XP close to Duradel.

unverified: Krystilia: the training guide says 'Any level (Done at least 1 task)', her own page says she refuses players still at level 1 Slayer, and the wiki's dialogue transcript is incomplete, so the exact rule is not confirmed
The order of the level 1 masters matters: with no rated method unlocked the app deals the last unlocked entry, so they run from Krystilia and Turael up to Nieve or Steve

Not included: Spria (same list as Turael plus sourhogs, needs A Porcine of Interest, cannot swap tasks) and Temple Trekking (5,800 to 7,800 Slayer XP an hour from reward tomes, needs In Aid of the Myreque; as the only rated low-level method it would drag every estimate down)

Duradel (both entries): no source gives XP an hour for any master; the bands are our own model, weighting the guides' per-task rates over his task list with six tasks blocked and none skipped, and allowing about five minutes between tasks; without a cannon that gives 16,000 at 50 rising to 28,500 at 93, at or under the ironman efficiency table's all-in rates (16,000, 21,000, 23,500, 24,200, 27,000, then 33,800 from 85); with cannon and barrage 33,000 from 65 and 36,000 from 93; a player who skips slow tasks does far better (62,000 to 87,000 by the same model, 74,250 to 93,000 in the main efficiency table), and the app assumes the player who does not

Every other master has no rate (xph 0): the app gives Slayer a stand-in rate by level in shared/data/fallback-rates.ts, taken from the same ironman efficiency table (5,000 an hour to level 49, then 16,000 to 28,500) and held at or under the Duradel figures; the main table's 12,000 at levels 40 to 49 is not used, so a main is estimated a little slow there
Mortimer: Fallen From Grace only has to be part done, which req cannot say, so req asks for the whole quest and is stricter than the game
